.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/orchi-epic.yml:
name: Orchi Epic
description: An independently verifiable outcome delivered as sequential Tasks on one branch and PR.
title: "[INITIATIVE][TAG] "
labels: [Epic]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: "Start the title with the Initiative tag and this Epic's own tag, for example [PAY][TOKEN] Tokenize stored cards. A standalone Epic uses only its own tag: [CSV] Export orders as CSV. Write it for an agent owner who has not seen the planning conversation: self-contained, concrete, and in plain language the user can also read and approve. A future Epic in an Initiative may answer a field with 'Deferred until #<n>: <reason>' only when the decision depends on that predecessor's result; see the Epic readiness checklist in Orchi's readiness reference (and the repository's own rules)."
  - type: textarea
    id: outcome
    attributes:
      label: Outcome
      description: The bounded result, not a list of components.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: sources
    attributes:
      label: Sources
      description: Authoritative documents, exact sections, and stable requirement/decision IDs; the parent Initiative when applicable.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: current
    attributes:
      label: Context and current state
      description: Why this outcome is needed and where it fits; evidence of the relevant current implementation (files, symbols, behavior) and the change needed.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: scope
    attributes:
      label: Scope
      description: In scope and out of scope.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: requirements
    attributes:
      label: Requirements
      description: Numbered requirements (R1, R2, ...) this Epic delivers, one per line, each traceable to a source or a recorded decision.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: design
    attributes:
      label: Design
      description: Approach, domain and interface decisions, data and ownership boundaries, invariants, test seams (where tests go and what each catches), and tradeoffs - and why this approach was chosen over the alternatives considered - or a link to them. State explicitly when there is no architecture change.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: ui
    attributes:
      label: UI design
      description: For an Epic that changes a user interface - its design depth (none, brief, or Epic); the surface brief link at depth brief; for a design Epic, the surfaces it designs, what must stay, and whether it replaces DESIGN.md; or the design Epic it is blocked by. Write "No user interface change" otherwise.
    validations:
      required: false
  - type: textarea
    id: decisions
    attributes:
      label: Decisions
      description: Each decision that shapes this Epic - the question, the answer, who decided (the user, or the main session under a cited user delegation), the date, and the reason. Quote the user's answers faithfully.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: surfaces
    attributes:
      label: Affected surfaces
      description: Code, schema, contract, test, and documentation areas expected to change.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: failure
    attributes:
      label: Failure and recovery
      description: Success and failure scenarios, inputs and outputs, risks, and the expected recovery behavior.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: branch
    attributes:
      label: Branch and PR
      description: The Epic branch and the PR target (the Initiative branch, or main for a standalone Epic). Record dependencies as native blocked-by relationships (in a new project, on its first run, except for a design Epic), and add the Tasks in execution order as native sub-issues.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: exit
    attributes:
      label: Exit criteria
      description: Observable acceptance mapped to requirements (R1 -> ...), each with its verification.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: questions
    attributes:
      label: Open questions
      description: Unresolved inputs, not presented as decided facts. Mark any question that affects the approach; the Epic is not ready for delivery until it is resolved.
  - type: textarea
    id: work
    attributes:
      label: Work reference
      description: Filled by the owner on claim - assistant session or identifier, branch, and PR.
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/orchi-exploration:
name: Orchi Exploration
description: An idea being researched and shaped with the user before any scope is planned.
title: "Explore: "
labels: [Exploration]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: "An exploration produces decisions, not code; Orchi's exploration reference defines its phases. Keep this body as the current map: write research findings and options as files in docs/work/<slug>/ on the explore/<slug> branch and link them here, and link prototype branches, which are never merged. When the user confirms the shape, the researcher crew continues into planning with this Issue; planning takes these decisions as agreed, so write them for a planner who has not seen the exploration conversation."
  - type: textarea
    id: destination
    attributes:
      label: Destination
      description: What is being decided, what the end of this exploration looks like, and how much the outcome is worth (Task, Epic, or Initiative size) and any time limit.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: request
    attributes:
      label: Original request
      description: The idea in the user's words, kept distinct from later decisions.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: constraints
    attributes:
      label: Constraints and no-gos
      description: Fixed limits, and what is explicitly out of scope (the exclusions).
  - type: textarea
    id: stack
    attributes:
      label: Stack
      description: For a new product - who uses it and on which devices, where it must run and what is mandated, how sensitive its data is, the hosting budget, and whether it is a proof of concept or meant to last; then the stack Orchi's standards defaults derive from them, with reasons. Leave empty otherwise.
    validations:
      required: false
  - type: textarea
    id: options
    attributes:
      label: Options
      description: Each direction considered - its shape, what it makes easy and hard, links to the research files it rests on - and the verdict with its reason.
  - type: textarea
    id: decisions
    attributes:
      label: Decisions
      description: Each decision with an id (D1, D2, ...) - the question, the answer, who decided, the date, the reason, and the area of the product it concerns. Quote the user's answers faithfully.
  - type: textarea
    id: requirements
    attributes:
      label: Requirements
      description: Numbered requirements (R1, R2, ...) of the chosen direction, each observable at completion.
  - type: textarea
    id: design
    attributes:
      label: Design
      description: For a product with a user interface - the screen map, the approved wireframe of each key screen, the references, the design engine, the approved comp, and the clickable mockup, each linked to its file in the working folder's design/, and the design board's link. Leave empty otherwise.
    validations:
      required: false
  - type: textarea
    id: shape
    attributes:
      label: Shape
      description: The chosen direction, and candidate Epics as outcomes, each with the result or contract it supplies to the next (the dependency between Epics).
  - type: textarea
    id: product
    attributes:
      label: Product
      description: For a product with a user interface - the primary users and their situation, the purpose and the mechanism no competitor shares, positioning, platform, stack (from the Stack field), constraints, brand commitments, evidence, and accessibility level (WCAG 2.2 AA unless the user says otherwise), for the first design Epic to record in PRODUCT.md. Leave empty otherwise.
    validations:
      required: false
  - type: textarea
    id: ideas
    attributes:
      label: Ideas
      description: Every idea the user raised and parked, and every direction, variant, or remark they turned down, each with why, so planning loses none.
    validations:
      required: false
  - type: textarea
    id: questions
    attributes:
      label: Open questions
      description: What is still open, each with what it blocks, the next one to ask first; list questions that can only be sensed so far as such.
  - type: textarea
    id: work
    attributes:
      label: Work reference
      description: The claim while someone holds this - the assignee's session or identifier, the branch, and the PR; in a pool, Orchi's `Assigned to crew-<k> (<session id>) by <Orchi> on <date>` line.
    validations:
      required: false
name: Orchi Initiative
description: A request decomposed into Epics on an initiative branch.
title: "[TAG] "
labels: [Initiative]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: "Replace TAG with this Initiative's own tag: 2-8 uppercase letters or digits that no other issue uses, for example [PAY] Card payments. Together with its plan document, the Initiative must pass the Initiative readiness checklist in Orchi's readiness reference before its first Epic starts. Write it for agent owners who have not seen the planning conversation."
  - type: textarea
    id: request
    attributes:
      label: Original request
      description: The request as agreed with the requester, kept distinct from later decisions.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: outcome
    attributes:
      label: Agreed outcome
      description: Observable result and explicit exclusions.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: requirements
    attributes:
      label: Requirements
      description: Numbered requirements (R1, R2, ...), one per line, each observable at completion.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: decisions
    attributes:
      label: Decisions
      description: Each decision that shapes this Initiative - the question, the answer, who decided (the user, or the main session under a cited user delegation), the date, and the reason. Quote the user's answers faithfully.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: epics
    attributes:
      label: Epic map
      description: Which Epic delivers each requirement, and each dependency between Epics explained through the result or contract it supplies. Epics themselves are native sub-issues.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: completion
    attributes:
      label: Integration and completion
      description: The integration branch, the completion criteria, and the final verification on the combined candidate.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: plan
    attributes:
      label: Plan
      description: Link to the working folder's plan, docs/work/<tag>-<slug>/README.md, on the initiative/<tag>-<slug> branch.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: work
    attributes:
      label: Work reference
      description: The claim while someone holds this - the assignee's session or identifier, the branch, and the PR; in a pool, Orchi's `Assigned to crew-<k> (<session id>) by <Orchi> on <date>` line.
    validations:
      required: false
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/orchi-task.yml:
name: Orchi Task
description: One reviewable result, either inside an Epic or as a standalone fix.
title: "[INITIATIVE][EPIC] "
labels: [Task]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: "Start the title with the same tags as the parent Epic, for example [PAY][TOKEN] Add token column, or [CSV] Add export endpoint under a standalone Epic. A standalone fix has no tags. The Task must pass the Task readiness checklist in Orchi's readiness reference (and the repository's own rules) before anyone starts it. Write it for an agent owner who has not seen the planning conversation: self-contained, concrete, and in plain language the user can also read and approve."
  - type: textarea
    id: outcome
    attributes:
      label: Outcome
      description: The one reviewable result this Task owns. Set the parent Epic as a native sub-issue relationship.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: context
    attributes:
      label: Context
      description: Why this result is needed and where it fits in the product or system; the relevant current behavior with code evidence (files and symbols, or path:line); and what later Tasks, Epics, or users consume from it (a contract, table, route, document section).
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: prerequisites
    attributes:
      label: Prerequisites
      description: Results that must already exist on the working branch, with Task or Epic references, or "None".
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: requirements
    attributes:
      label: Requirements
      description: Numbered requirements (R1, R2, ...), one per line, each individually verifiable. Use "must" and "must not", and cite the stable requirement IDs they implement when the project has them.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: vision
    attributes:
      label: Solution vision
      description: The intended approach and the likely change points - code symbols, routes, migrations, tables, contracts, tests, and documentation - and why this approach was chosen over the alternatives considered. Guidance for the owner, not a permission list.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: ui
    attributes:
      label: UI design
      description: For a Task that changes a user interface - the design depth (none, brief, or Epic), the design engine (Hallmark or prototype, as DESIGN.md names it), the DESIGN.md sections it follows, the surface brief and the approved comp it builds against, and the states, breakpoints, themes, and accessibility level it covers. Write "No user interface change" otherwise.
    validations:
      required: false
  - type: textarea
    id: decisions
    attributes:
      label: Decisions
      description: Each decision that shapes this Task - the question, the answer, who decided (the user, or the main session under a cited user delegation), the date, and the reason. Quote the user's answers faithfully. Write "None needed" if nothing had to be decided.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: sources
    attributes:
      label: Sources
      description: Exact design sections, documents, requirement/decision IDs, and the code or issues inspected while planning. Link sections, not whole documents.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: constraints
    attributes:
      label: Constraints and non-goals
      description: Invariants, boundaries, and what this Task must not change or attempt.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: scenarios
    attributes:
      label: Scenarios
      description: Concrete success scenarios and failure scenarios (invalid input, missing data, conflicts, unavailable dependencies) with the expected behavior of each. For a defect, the reproduction command that has already failed on the reported symptom, or why none exists and which evidence replaces it.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: acceptance
    attributes:
      label: Acceptance and verification
      description: Observable behavior mapped to the requirements (R1 -> ...), the exact checks or commands that establish it, and the seams where new tests go, with an existing test to follow. State user-facing behavior as what a user can see or do, each with its acceptance test (until the acceptance harness lands, and in a proof of concept, what the running app shows); take the checks from ENGINEERING.md when it exists.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: docs
    attributes:
      label: Documentation impact
      description: Owning pages to update (per the project's documentation routing - the ownership map in docs/README.md by default), including a behavior page for a change a user can see, or why no documentation changes.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: writer
    attributes:
      label: Suggested writer
      description: Optional. Whether the change is small and fully determined by this Issue (orchi-fixer) or needs orchi-implementer, and why. The delivering session makes the final choice.
  - type: textarea
    id: questions
    attributes:
      label: Open questions
      description: Unresolved inputs, not presented as decided facts. Resolve any question that affects this Task's approach, or move it to a bounded investigation Task, before anyone starts it.
  - type: textarea
    id: work
    attributes:
      label: Work reference
      description: For a standalone Task, filled by the owner on claim - assistant session or identifier, branch, and PR.
.github/github-app.yml:
instructions: |
  This repository runs its work through Orchi. Follow the Orchi workflow section of AGENTS.md and the
  orchi-core skill of the orchi plugin (orchi@orchi-copilot).
.github/pull_request_template.md:
<!-- orchi:begin -->
## Summary

<!-- What changed and why. Link issues; closing keywords only work for PRs into the default branch. -->

## Verification

<!-- Commands, results, red evidence for new tests, and the candidate commit. Each acceptance claim: established, limited, or not established. Before/after output or screenshots for a visible change. -->

## Merge risk

<!-- One-way door (hard to undo) or two-way door (a revert undoes it), and the blast radius if it is wrong. -->

## Exceptions

<!-- Each ENGINEERING.md exception this PR adds or changes, in plain words: what is waived, where, why, and until when. Otherwise: None. -->

## Documentation impact

<!-- Required: the pages updated, or why no documentation changes. The Orchi documentation check fails when this is empty. -->

## Handoff

<!-- Only while work is interrupted: branch/commit, done, remaining, uncommitted changes, checks, next step. -->
<!-- orchi:end -->
.github/workflows/orchi-docs.yml:
name: Orchi documentation

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, reopened, synchronize]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  documentation:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Check for new broken documentation links
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: python3 .github/orchi/scripts/knowledge.py lint --since "origin/$BASE_REF"
      - name: Check the Documentation impact section
        if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'
        env:
          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
        run: python3 .github/orchi/scripts/knowledge.py impact
      - name: Keep working documents out of the default branch
        if: github.base_ref == github.event.repository.default_branch
        run: python3 .github/orchi/scripts/knowledge.py work
.github/workflows/orchi-standards.yml:
name: Orchi standards

on:
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  standards:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Check that every check ENGINEERING.md declares runs in CI
        run: python3 .github/orchi/scripts/standards.py check

  drift:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Keep one Issue that lists what drifted
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          status=0
          findings=$(python3 .github/orchi/scripts/standards.py check 2>&1) || status=$?
          echo "$findings"
          [ "$status" -eq 0 ] && exit 0
          title="Standards drift"
          number=$(gh issue list --state open --label needs-planning --json number,title \
            --jq ".[] | select(.title == \"$title\") | .number" | head -n 1)
          body=$(printf 'The weekly `standards.py check` found:\n\n```\n%s\n```\n\nPlan this like any request.\n' "$findings")
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue edit "$number" --body "$body"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$title" --label needs-planning --body "$body"
          fi
.gitignore:
# orchi:begin
# Temporary files of Orchi's sessions and subagents.
.orchi-tmp/
# orchi:end
AGENTS.md:
<!-- orchi:begin -->
## Orchi workflow

Orchi runs this repository's work: the user talks to the Orchi Copilot Project, or types `/orchi`, and Orchi routes each request to a session for its role.
Orchi, its sessions, and their subagents follow the `orchi-core` skill of the `orchi` plugin (`orchi@orchi-copilot`). Anywhere else, answer questions only, and ask the user to bring work to Orchi.
Research first and agree the outcome, approach, and scope (Task, Epic, or Initiative) with the user before creating branches, issues, or changes.
Track work in Git branches and GitHub Issues; resume from the existing issue, branch, and PR instead of duplicating work.
For documentation-only questions, use its retrieval guidance without creating tracking.
Where `ENGINEERING.md` exists, follow it and run its checks; never weaken a check without recording an exception there.
`docs/README.md`, when present, maps the current documentation; working documents live in `docs/work/` on branches and never reach main.
Do not infer merge or deployment permission from permission to implement.
<!-- orchi:end -->
